title: Receipt Allowance Charge on Posted Retail Receipts
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit, over-the-counter allowance.** When a transmitted retail pharmacy register receipt is posted, the receipt allowance charge is the part of its register total charged to the member's allowance.

**Rule.** The receipt allowance charge is nine tenths (0.9) of the register total of the transmitted receipt, the remaining tenth being treated as sales tax and non-catalog items, and it never exceeds the allowance balance at posting.

### Order of working

1. Take the register total of the receipt being posted.
2. Multiply it by nine tenths (90 percent); the remaining tenth is treated as sales tax and non-catalog items.
3. Limit the product to the allowance balance at posting — the coverage's current allowance balance at the moment of posting.
4. Round the receipt allowance charge to the cent. Only this final figure is rounded.

### Worked figures (hypothetical)

| Register total | Nine tenths | Allowance balance at posting | Receipt allowance charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| $40.00 | $36.00 | $50.00 | $36.00 |
| $40.00 | $36.00 | $30.00 | $30.00 |
| $23.47 | $21.123 | $50.00 | $21.12 |

In the second row the balance at posting is the lower figure, so the charge is $30.00. In the third row the product is carried unrounded and only the charge is rounded, to $21.12.
